Pilot gift bundles that make sense: three small combinations

Build a small pilot gift bundle around one clear purpose. These combinations use listed prices and leave room to check compatibility, tax and delivery.

By Pilot Gift Guide · From the team behind ATC · How we choose

IN THIS GUIDEFor a student who wants paper basicsFor a practical flight-bag refreshFor an off-duty aviation fanKeep the total honestThe gift shortlist

For a student who wants paper basics

An ASA logbook at $9.49 and SKILCRAFT B3 pen at $24.50 total $33.99 before tax and shipping. This is a sensible pairing only if the student wants that logbook format and pen. Ask the instructor or recipient first. Add a note celebrating the start of training, rather than filling the package with accessories that have no role in the student’s current lessons.

For a practical flight-bag refresh

The Aviator’s Light at $29.95 and B3 pen at $24.50 total $54.45 before delivery and tax. The shared purpose is easy access to two small tools, but the pilot may already own preferred versions. Confirm that both would be welcome. A bundle is not automatically better value than one item; its value comes from the recipient using what is inside.

For an off-duty aviation fan

A Cessna cap at $34.99 and Blue Angels ornament at $17.99 total $52.98 before tax and shipping. These are different aviation interests, so combine them only for someone who likes both. Otherwise choose one item and a personal card. Do not manufacture a theme simply because two products have airplanes on them.

Keep the total honest

Prices in these examples were checked on October 20, 2026. Separate retailers may charge separate shipping fees, and a modest bundle can exceed a firm budget at checkout. Keep the receipts for each item and avoid splitting a digital gift-card code across a public group chat. If your target is a fixed delivered total, leave a buffer rather than spending every dollar on merchandise.

The gift shortlist

Open the retailer listing for current prices, specifications and delivery. Prices below were checked October 20, 2026.

Under $25

SKILCRAFT B3 Aviator pen

$24.50

Black ink, red ink and a pencil in one everyday tool. An uncomplicated addition to a practical gift bundle, especially with a handwritten note.

Buying tips

Check whether they prefer paper notes; an all-digital pilot may get less use from it.

For a first lesson

ASA pilot logbook

$9.49

An affordable way to mark the start of flight training. Pair it with a note about the journey ahead, rather than filling in any flight-record pages yourself.

Buying tips

Check with their instructor first: they may already have a logbook or use a different format.

A useful little extra

Flight Gear Aviator’s Light

$29.95

A compact light with separate red and white controls. It makes sense for the person who likes keeping small, useful tools in their flight bag.

Buying tips

Ask what light they already carry; this is an accessory, not a replacement for required equipment.

View at Sporty’s ↗
Off-duty aviation

Cessna patch trucker cap

$34.99

A casual option for the Cessna enthusiast who already owns the flight gear they need. The navy-and-scarlet color scheme makes it easy to wear away from the airport.

Buying tips

Confirm they like caps and Cessna; a familiar logo is more personal than a random airplane.
